feedback: Approved as a clean single-variable test of the best raced design. Iteration 5 (sensors at x = -0.05 to 0.05, y = 0.07, sensor_size 0.012, kp 1.5, ki 0.5, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.2, last_direction) scored 417.25, with oval 20 of 20 finished and s-bend progress 0.56. Iteration 6 changed only sensor_size to 0.016 and scored 350.07, with oval finish falling to 0.9 and slalom progress to 0.12, so the larger footprint is refuted and this candidate reverts it to 0.012. Iteration 4 showed that widening the outer sensors to ±0.07 hurt (271.70), so the x spread stays at ±0.05. Slalom has shown exactly 1 line-loss event per run at a fixed point across iterations 3 to 6 with progress stuck near 0.19, and changing sensor coverage has not moved it, which points to the recovery behaviour. This candidate changes only controller.line_loss, from last_direction to search_right (signal fixed at +1, steering left on loss), so any effect is isolated. Read the race in this order. (1) If slalom progress rises above 0.2 and its line_loss_events stay at or near 1 per run, keep search_right and test search_left next only if the drift direction is to the right. (2) If slalom progress drops or is unchanged, search_right is not helping, so the next test is controller.line_loss search_left on the same geometry. (3) If oval or s-bend results differ materially from iteration 5 (oval finish below 1.0, s-bend progress below 0.5), the recovery mode is affecting the normal line-following path, so revert to last_direction and keep the iteration 5 design as the baseline.
requested_changes: Keep the iteration 5 geometry (sensor_size 0.012, sensor x = -0.05, -0.025, 0, 0.025, 0.05 at y = 0.07) and set controller.line_loss to search_left only if this race shows slalom progress unchanged or lower with search_right, since iterations 3 to 6 showed the slalom loss is a fixed-point recovery problem and sensor coverage alone has not stopped it.

If slalom progress rises above 0.2 with search_right and oval finish stays at 1.0, keep line_loss search_right and try controller.base_speed 1.4 with the other fields unchanged, since iteration 5 showed the oval is stable at speed 1.2 and speed has not been tested on the tight tracks at this geometry.

If oval finish falls below 0.8 or oval steering_oscillation rises above about 0.25 with search_right, revert controller.line_loss to last_direction and keep the iteration 5 baseline, since the recovery mode is then disturbing normal line following.
